draft.title: Scalars and vectors
card: a quantity with size only, such as distance, speed, mass and time. It is fully described by a number and a unit.
a quantity with size and direction, such as displacement, velocity and force. A full description needs a number, a unit and a direction.
Direction can be given in words, such as north or upwards, or by a sign, such as + and - along a line. Opposite directions have opposite signs.
A vector keeps its direction in the answer. 50 km/h is a speed. 50 km/h east is a velocity.
draft.remember: If a quantity needs a direction to be complete, it is a vector. If not, it is a scalar.

opts: A force of 20 N downwards
A mass of 20 kg
A time of 20 s
A speed of 20 m/s
a.why: A force of 20 N downwards has a size and a direction, so it is a vector. A speed of 20 m/s is tempting, but it gives size only, so it is a scalar.
a.clue: Which one is given with a direction?

b.q: Priya cycles at 12 m/s around a circular track. Which statement about her motion is correct?
opts: 12 m/s is her speed, as no direction is given
12 m/s is her velocity, as it has a size
12 m/s is her speed, as she travels in a circle
12 m/s is her velocity, as it is measured in m/s
b.why: The value 12 m/s has a size only, with no direction stated, so it is a speed, which is a scalar. Units of m/s do not decide it: a velocity must also include a direction.
b.clue: Does the value 12 m/s include a direction?

b.best: 12 m/s is her speed, as no direction is given

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one with a qualifier (a direction), so a student could pick the odd one out without knowing the idea. A distractor that also carries extra detail would make it a fairer test.
